scope: Corollary 7.5 (Cuspidal comparison across coefficient primes) of the manuscript “Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration” (preprints/Rationality-of-the-Canonical-Unramified-Arthur-Filtration-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eaf8e38720714e23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Keep the curve X/Fq, the split connected semisimple group G/Fq, and all four conditions of Assumption 1.1. Put p = char(Fq) and Eℓ = Qℓ for ℓ ̸= p. At unramified level D = 0, let C0,Q ⊂ AQ be the cuspidal function space and C0,O,Q its rational orbit summands from [RA, Theorem 1.1], and set C0,ℓ = Eℓ ⊗Q C0,Q. For each ℓ ̸= p, let Yℓ ⊂ c NEℓ be closed and invariant, with the same nilpotent-orbit subset Y under the fixed pinned split rational dual group. Write Y = (Yℓ)ℓ̸=p and define FQ Y,ℓ := AQ ∩ FYℓ AEℓ , VY,Q := M O∈Y C0,O,Q. Then C0,Q ∩ FQ Y,ℓ = VY,Q, C0,ℓ ∩ FYℓ AEℓ = Eℓ ⊗Q VY,Q. (7.1) The intersections are taken in the corresponding finitely supported function spaces. The equalities include the zero cusp space and empty or full Yℓ.
